correctness.rationale: Two necessary obstructions are established by a cluster-preserving automorphism and a cross-cluster color bisimulation. Explicit recursively constructed modal formulas isolate every suffix, then every singleton. Counting is a right-to-left product of admissible palettes and within-cluster bijections; positivity gives the exact binary-pattern rank. The proof covers all positive size vectors and r>=0 and is independently checked computationally on 1,035,339 colorings, 411 complete finite censuses, and 5,606 direct modal algebra closures.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The general cluster bound is necessary but not sufficient for generation; consecutive nondecreasing cluster sizes can force one additional binary pattern. Definability under a preexisting full-generation hypothesis does not imply the claimed decision criterion or enumerator. General bisimulation theory is a tool, not broader numerical coverage.

value.rationale: A natural full classification and exact invariant for finite S4.3 frame algebras. The sharp additional color needed across nondecreasing adjacent clusters is not given by the standard per-cluster size bound. The product census and explicit singleton construction solve minimal generator and counting questions for every finite size vector, without expensive term closure. These are substantive finite modal-algebra data beyond a textbook closure or special-case numerical check.
